messages:
maria: heads-up — installer zip on linux + umask 027 is leaving redwoodctl without exec bit. localtest can't run and login hangs.

alex: oof. can you paste the ls -l from the extracted dir?

maria: sure
```
$ ls -l ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl
-rw-r--r-- 1 maria staff 123456 Mar 20 10:01 redwoodctl
```

sam: that explains it. installer assumes chmod +x but zip extraction under some package managers preserves perms. umask 027 removes exec.

maria: workaround: `chmod +x ~/.local/bin/redwoodctl` fixed it. but this trips new users during quickstart (localtest). auth flow just times out.

ben: could also detect at postinstall and run `chmod` automatically. if it's a casked install we should avoid elevating perms.

alex: filing quick PR to add a sanity check in postinstall and a warning if file not executable. adding a smoke test to CI that runs `redwoodctl --version` after install.

maria: thanks. also saw `redwoodctl login` fails with `authentication retry: no response` — probably because the companion browser flow never launched due to CLI not executable.

deploy-bot: deploy check: created issue #3412 for postinstall chmod + smoke test

sam: assign to @alex. also add note to docs: `If you installed via unzip and see permission errors, run chmod +x` and include WSL corner-case.

alex: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/pull/789 — adds postinstall check + doc snippet. will run CI after review.

maria: confirmed fix works for me on ubuntu 22.04 + WSL2. localtest onboarding smoother now :thumbsup: 

ben: follow-up: we should add telemetry for first-run exec errors (opt-in). created follow-up issue #3413.

maria: leaving this thread here in case others hit it. thanks team.
